subject: Geography
central_question: What is biodiversity, why does it matter, what threatens it, and how can conservation protect the living systems on which humans depend?
in_scope_units: Biodiversity and its uneven global distribution
Conservation, mega diversity centres and hotspots
Protected areas, law, international action and community involvement
banned_topics: Detailed ecosystem structure and food-chain theory from the preceding chapter
Detailed geomorphic weathering beyond its brief link to vegetation diversity
Modern threatened-species categories not stated in the supplied chapter

known_pitfalls.claim: Biodiversity means only the number of animal species.
known_pitfalls.correction: It includes plants, animals, microorganisms, genes and ecosystems and is discussed at three levels.

known_pitfalls.claim: Areas with larger populations necessarily have greater species diversity.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter says biodiversity is richer in the tropics and declines toward the poles.

known_pitfalls.claim: Conservation is only about protecting individual endangered species.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter stresses habitat protection, sustainable use, local participation and continuity of conservation.

known_pitfalls.claim: Exotic species are rare native species.
known_pitfalls.correction: They are introduced organisms that are not natural inhabitants of the local habitat.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 3(ii): analyse biodiversity loss and prevention
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1, 2 and 3 and Project Work on mapping national parks, sanctuaries and biosphere reserves.
